sentences.text: Being aggrieved by the impugned award, the appellants/claimants have preferred this appeal on the ground that the learned Claims Tribunal passed the impugned award without proper appreciation of law.
It is contended that the compensation awarded is on the lower side.
Prior to the alleged accident, deceased was a healthy person aged around 30 years and was engaged in the work of driver.
However, the learned Claims Tribunal failed to consider these aspects and assessed the income of the deceased extremely low.
It is further submitted that income of the deceased must be assessed as per Minimum Wages Act of skilled labour at the time of accident.
It is further contended that Claims Tribunal has committed error in not adding future prospects and not awarding reasonable amount of compensation in other conventional heads.
Hence, it is prayed that reasonable amount of compensation may be awarded to the claimants.
7. On the other hand, learned counsels for the Insurance Company supported the impugned award and prayed for rejection of the appeal.

8. Heard learned counsel for the parties and perused the record of the Claims Tribunal.
9.

With regard to the assessment of income, the learned Claims Tribunal assessed the income of the deceased at Rs.3,200/- per month on the ground that no documentary evidence regarding his income was produced.
However, the record reflects that the deceased was engaged in driver work and the claimants have produced sufficient material in support thereof.
In the considered opinion of this Court, the income of the deceased ought to be assessed in accordance with the Minimum Wages applicable to a skilled worker.

Therefore, in considered opinion NEUTRAL CITATION NO.
2026:MPHC-GWL:10654 3 MA-980-2011 of this Court, the just and proper amount of the income of the deceased as a skilled person as per Minimum Wages Act in the present case is Rs.3,800/- per month.

10. As regard to loss of income including future prospects, in the light of judgment of National Insurance Co. Ltd. Vs. Pranay Sethi, 2017 ACJ 2700, the claimants are entitled for loss of income including future prospects.

entities.text: National Insurance Co. Ltd. Vs. Pranay Sethi, 2017 ACJ 2700
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: As per Pranay Sethi (supra), future prospects @ 40% be assessed.

Further, as per the judgment of the Apex Court in the case of Sarla Verma and ors. Vs Delhi Transport Corporation and Anr. reported in (2009) 6 SCC 121 , even if age of the deceased is to be taken into account, multiplier of 17 has rightly been applied by Claims Tribunal.
